title: Segue & ColorGuard: Optimizing SFI Performance and Scalability on Modern Architectures
problem: Software-based fault isolation (SFI) for WebAssembly (Wasm) incurs significant performance overhead from memory-access instrumentation and limits the number of Wasm instances that can run concurrently in a single address space due to address-space partitioning constraints.
motivation: Wasm sandboxing is critical for safe, high-performance web and server-side execution, but its instrumentation overhead and scalability limits are barriers to broad deployment in latency-sensitive and high-concurrency applications.
method: Segue exploits x86-64 segment registers (FS/GS base) to encode sandbox memory bounds directly in hardware, eliminating the explicit bounds-check instrumentation instructions for most memory accesses; this removes 44.7% of Wasm overhead on a Wasm-compatible SPEC CPU 2006 subset and reduces font-rendering sandbox overhead in Firefox by 75%. ColorGuard leverages memory protection keys (MPK/memory tagging) to color each Wasm instance's memory region with a distinct tag, enabling up to 15x more concurrent Wasm instances in a single address space without requiring separate address spaces.
key_novelty: Using x86-64 segment registers as hardware-enforced sandbox bounds to eliminate SFI instrumentation overhead, combined with memory protection key coloring for 15x concurrency scaling.
contributions: Segue: exploiting x86-64 segmentation to eliminate up to 44.7% of Wasm SFI overhead on SPEC CPU 2006 and 75% on Firefox font rendering.
ColorGuard: memory-tagging-based Wasm instance coloring enabling up to 15x more concurrent instances per address space.
Integration and evaluation of both optimizations in three production Wasm toolchains: Wasm2c, WAMR, and Wasmtime.

metrics.speedup: eliminates 44.7% of Wasm overhead on SPEC CPU 2006 subset; reduces Firefox Wasm font rendering overhead by 75%
metrics.other: up to 15x more concurrent Wasm instances per address space

limitations: Segue relies on x86-64 segmentation registers that are not available on ARM; portability to non-x86 architectures is limited.
primary_theme: Hardware-assisted SFI performance and scalability for WebAssembly via segmentation and memory tagging
